Add specs, and hide technical functions from the docs changed since 93873be and was graded against the current text. The sentences that decide the verdict: "Give every public function a `@spec`, including functions marked `@doc false` and functions a macro defines in the caller's module" and "A function that implements a `@callback` under `@impl` needs none; the callback carries the types." (library-design.md, line 61). sonnet-2's @doc false Forecast.parse/1 has a @spec (line 149); the Exception message/1 in sonnet-1 (line 26) and sonnet-2 (line 186) sits under @impl true without a @spec, which is allowed. No run defines functions in a macro. All four runs are clean.

The compiles entries in result.json were ignored as instructed. They do not all fail on Req: sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 compile with warnings about the missing Req modules, while haiku-1 and haiku-2 fail because WeatherClient builds %Error{} (haiku-1 line 103, haiku-2 line 88) before the file defines WeatherClient.Error. Not graded.

Naming was not counted for sonnet-1's fetch_forecast/3, which returns {:error, %Error{}}, or haiku-2's private get/3: both name HTTP requests, not key lookups, which is what the get/fetch bullet (with its new sentence on key lookups) governs.
